name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deeply Republican district with a +21 Republican partisan lean
First-term incumbent Mark Alford running with a large financial advantage
Democrat Jordan Herrera has raised only about $42,000 with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 6 percent
model.rationale: This central Missouri seat sits about 21 points to the right of the country, and incumbent Mark Alford is seeking a second term with roughly $1.4 million raised against about $42,000 for Jordan Herrera. With no public polling, no expert ratings, and markets giving Democrats only a small chance, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a polling error of historic size in rural Missouri, would be needed to put this race in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 4th District is a strongly Republican seat, and first-term Representative Mark Alford is running for reelection with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant fundraising position. He has raised about $1.4 million and holds over $747,000 on hand, while Democrat Jordan Herrera has raised roughly $42,000 and entered the fall with under $20,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any reported fundraising.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's heavy Republican lean and the resource gap. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 6 percent chance. An upset would require a dramatic shift in the political environment or a major influx of outside money on the Democratic side, neither of which is currently visible.
